classification.difficultyReason: Evaluate a power-rule improper integral, reuse its area to verify a PDF, and integrate to obtain and sketch the CDF; the sequence explicitly supplies the connections.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Find the area under the curve $y=\dfrac{1}{x^2}$ over the interval $(1,\infty)$.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Hence show that $y=\dfrac{1}{x^2}$ for $x\ge1$ is a PDF, and find the CDF.

answer.short:
$f(x)\ge0$ for $x\ge1$ and its total area is $1$, so it is a PDF.
$$F(x)=\begin{cases}0,&x<1,\\1-\dfrac1x,&x\ge1.\end{cases}$$
answer.worked:
$f(x)=\dfrac1{x^2}\ge0$ for all $x\ge1$, and part a shows that the integral over $[1,\infty)$ is $1$. Therefore it is a PDF, taking $f(x)=0$ for $x<1$.
For $x\ge1$:
$$\begin{align*}F(x)&=\int_1^x\frac1{t^2}\,dt\\&=\left[-\frac1t\right]_1^x\\&=-\frac1x-(-1)\\&=1-\frac1x.\end{align*}$$
For $x<1$, $F(x)=0$.

children.label: c
children.prompt: Sketch the PDF and CDF on two separate sets of axes.

answer.short: $f(x)=\dfrac1{x^2}$ for $x\ge1$: starts at $(1,1)$ and decreases towards $y=0$.
answer.worked: Plot the closed point $(1,1)$. Sketch $f(x)=\dfrac1{x^2}$ decreasing and concave up for $x\ge1$, approaching the horizontal asymptote $y=0$. The shaded area under this curve is $1$.

spec.description: PDF sketch with a closed point at (1,1), horizontal guide, vertical boundary and the requested shaded area.
spec.mathematics: f(x)=1/x^2 for x>=1; integral from 1 to infinity equals 1; horizontal asymptote y=0.

answer.short: $F(x)=1-\dfrac1x$ for $x\ge1$: starts at $(1,0)$ and increases towards $y=1$.
answer.worked: Plot the closed point $(1,0)$. Sketch $F(x)=1-\dfrac1x$ increasing and concave down for $x\ge1$, approaching the horizontal asymptote $F(x)=1$. For $x<1$, $F(x)=0$.

spec.description: CDF sketch with a closed point at (1,0), increasing concave-down curve and dashed horizontal asymptote at 1. The zero branch coincides with the horizontal axis.
spec.mathematics: F(x)=0 for x<1 and F(x)=1-1/x for x>=1; limit at infinity is 1.
